With the unanimous support OF
mere than 300 residents, the American
University Park Citizens Association
today was on record as opposed to
elimination of the Massachusetts, ave-
nue. bus line and against ending direct
through bus service from its area to
the downtown section, as proposed
recently by the Capital Transit Co.


In q resolution adopted last night
by the largest group ever to attend
one of its meetings, the association
vigorously opposed any change at all
in the present bus route between
American University Park and Eight
zenith street and Pennsylvania avenue.


Thomas E. Lodge, delegate to the
Federation of Citizens Associations,
informed the group the Public Utilities
Commission has filed the proposal.


Would End Direct Service.


The railway company's proposal.
Lodge said, would establish the east
terminal of the line at the Bureau OF
Standards and the west terminal at
Western avenue and Butternut street,
thus eliminating entirely the direct
service, via Massachusetts, avenue, to
the downtown area.


The association declared in the
resolution. the effects of this change
would be to isolate American Univer-
sity Park residents from the Wesley
Heights section, the public schools
and the university. The proposal to
route buses to Wisconsin avenue via
River road would make it necessary
for residents to find a new shopping
center, as the area near Forty first
and Fessenden streets, now used for
that purpose, would be cut of.


Peoples Counsel William A. Roberts
discussed several alternate plans
which have been suggested, but in
formed the association he will fight
for whatever plan the residents
wanted He described several rerout-
ing changes which will be made.


Ask Buses Be Marked.


The association also requested the
buses to American University Park
be so marked rather than simply
Wesley Heights.


In another proposal the group re-
quested the Commissioners to secure
a site for an elementary school IN
the park section.


President William T. Belts presided
over the meeting, which was held in
Hurst Hall, at American University.
